- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is trending upward for 5+ days, forecast often fails to correct; apply slight downward adjustment after 5-day uptrend.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 30-day moving average if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often ignores recent auction supply events; if supply net is negative and recent auctions are scheduled, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per event.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility; apply volatility-adjusted buffer (±1.5–2.5%) to forecast range.
